problem: Lagrangian-based safe fine-tuning of VLAs (e.g., SafeVLA) enforces safety only softly on expected cumulative cost, leaving residual violations or conservative behavior through a persistent reward-cost trade-off. Dense per-step safety labels are also unavailable in visual domains, and free-form VLM judgments are too noisy.
motivation: Safety-critical robots need per-state feasibility reasoning rather than a global penalty. HJ reachability offers a worst-case safe-set characterization that can be learned model-free, and structured rubric VLM scoring can supply per-frame supervision from only episode-level outcome bits.
key_idea: Learn a model-free Hamilton-Jacobi reachability safety critic from VLM-rubric-derived margins and use it as a hard gate: reward PPO gradient in feasible states, safety-value ascent (-Q_s) in infeasible states.
insight: Decoupling reward and safety via the gate matters: replacing the gate with a Lagrangian penalty using the same critic and rubric drops TurtleBot-Nav SR from 0.54 to 0.33 and raises CSC from 6.90 to 7.80. Continuous rubric margins matter more than binary collision costs for task success (TurtleBot SR 0.54 vs 0.31, Franka SR 0.45 vs 0.25), though binary costs give lower CSC in some environments. Scorer capacity is a bottleneck (2B scorer mode-collapses; 8B plus RTD rubrics lifts tail AUROC from 0.500 to 0.608).
method: HJ safety critic: off-policy Q_s(o,a) trained with the discounted HJ safety Bellman target y=(1-γ)ℓ+γ·min{ℓ, Q̄(o',a')} on a shared replay buffer, concurrently with the policy (K=4 steps per PPO iteration, Polyak target)
Feasibility-gated loss: ζ=1[Q_s(o,ā_θ(o))>δ]; L = ζ·L_PPO + β_t(1-ζ)·(-Q_s(o,ā_θ)), with stop-gradient on the gate
Dual ascent on β_t: β is updated from the mean episode cost versus budget c_max, applied only to infeasible transitions
Rubric VLM margin: frozen Qwen3-VL-8B scores each frame on K anchored rubrics (proximity, heading, contact, occlusion, clearance) in [0,1]; the weighted sum gives raw severity ρ
Platt calibration: class-balanced logistic regression on ρ against the broadcast per-episode safety bit gives ℓ̂=-(aρ+b); no per-step labels needed
Refinement-through-Differentiation (RTD): offline loop where a 72B proposer VLM invents new rubrics from disagreement pairs, fixing tail failures

Critic architecture: independent module with a vision encoder (initialized from the VLA encoder) and an MLP Q-head over feature plus action; twin critic for Franka-Reach; single policy deployed with no runtime shield

setting.backbone: OmniVLA (TurtleBot-Nav), SPOC-based VLA (Safety-CHORES), OpenVLA-OFT (Franka-Reach), ResNet-18+CLIP controller (Dubins-VL); all fine-tuned with PPO; Qwen3-VL-8B frozen scorer during training only
setting.model_size: OpenVLA-OFT (~7B); Qwen3-VL-8B scorer; Qwen2.5-VL-72B proposer for RTD only
setting.training_data: Online RL interaction in simulation (1M-25M steps per environment), BC-initialized pretrained VLAs; VLM rubric scores on rollout frames plus per-episode safety bits for calibration
setting.observation: Egocentric or top-down RGB (dual egocentric RGB for Safety-CHORES, wrist/front RGB for Franka), plus language instruction
setting.action_space: Continuous velocity (Dubins, TurtleBot, Franka EE delta) and 20 discrete primitives (Safety-CHORES)
setting.privileged: none at test time; GT cost used only in the oracle HJ (GT cost) baseline on Dubins-VL; simulator contact used for evaluation only

numbers.extra: 3 seeds mean reported in Table 3; 200 eval episodes

numbers_note: SR here means Safe+Reach (goal reached with zero violations). CSC is the paper's cumulative safety cost. Benchmarks are custom or Safety-CHORES rather than standard navigation benchmarks; split is not specified in the paper, so 'test' is used as the closest label.
results: Across five environments ShieldVLA lowers CSC by 57% on average and raises SR by +0.13 over SafeVLA. It reaches, for example, SR 0.68/CSC 1.44 on S-CHORES Nav versus SafeVLA 0.59/1.82, and SR 0.54/CSC 6.90 on TurtleBot-Nav versus SafeVLA 0.34/14.6. It also degrades more gracefully under color and lighting shifts, with the lowest CSC in every OOD cell.
limitations: Safety claims are empirical only: contraction guarantees don't carry over to function approximation, and the VLM rubric adds error on top of the critic's
Depends on VLM scorer capacity (sub-8B scorers mode-collapse) and on sufficient near-boundary exploration; δ becomes hand-tuned when unsafe events are rare
Simulation only, with a single published baseline (SafeVLA) and no real-robot validation
builds_on: Rubric-based rewards / Chasing the Tail (Zhang et al. 2025)
